from manim import *

class QueueVisualization(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Container
        title = Text("Queue (FIFO: First-In-First-Out)", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # Create an open-ended horizontal container
        top_line = Line(LEFT * 3, RIGHT * 3).shift(UP * 0.6)
        bottom_line = Line(LEFT * 3, RIGHT * 3).shift(DOWN * 0.6)
        self.add(top_line, bottom_line)

        front_label = Text("FRONT", font_size=20, color=GREY_A).next_to(top_line.get_left(), UP, buff=0.1)
        back_label = Text("BACK", font_size=20, color=GREY_A).next_to(top_line.get_right(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(front_label, back_label)

        # 2. Enqueue Operation (Items enter from the BACK/RIGHT)
        queue_items = VGroup()
        item_labels = ["A", "B", "C"]
        colors = [RED, GREEN, BLUE]

        for i, (label, color) in enumerate(zip(item_labels, colors)):
            # Create item square
            square = Square(side_length=0.8, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5)
            text = Text(label, font_size=24)
            item = VGroup(square, text)
            
            # Move item from outside the BACK to its position in the queue
            item.move_to(RIGHT * 5) 
            target_pos = LEFT * (1.5 - i * 1.0) 
            
            self.play(
                item.animate.move_to(target_pos),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            queue_items.add(item)
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Dequeue Operation (Item exits from the FRONT/LEFT)
        dequeued_item = queue_items[0]
        self.play(
            dequeued_item.animate.move_to(LEFT * 5),
            # Shift remaining items forward
            queue_items[1].animate.move_to(LEFT * 1.5),
            queue_items[2].animate.move_to(LEFT * 0.5),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(dequeued_item))
        
        self.play(Indicate(queue_items[1], color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(top_line, bottom_line, front_label, back_label, queue_items[1:], title)))

class MeanCalculation(Scene):

Label each with its name and degree range (e.g., '< 90', '= 90', '> 90') to illustrate basic geometric terminology.

from manim import *

class AngleClassification(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Classification of Angles", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(title))

        # Helper to create an angle with label
        def create_labeled_angle(angle_deg, name, math_desc, include_arc=True):
            l1 = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE)
            l2 = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE).rotate(angle_deg * DEGREES, about_point=ORIGIN)
            
            res = VGroup(l1, l2)
            if include_arc:
                angle_arc = Angle(l1, l2, radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
                res.add(angle_arc)
            
            label_name = Text(name, font_size=24).next_to(l1, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            label_math = Text(math_desc, font_size=20, color=GREY_A).next_to(label_name, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            res.add(label_name, label_math)
            
            return res

        # 2. Define Angles and Positions
        acute = create_labeled_angle(45, "Acute", "< 90°").move_to(LEFT * 4 + DOWN * 0.5)
        right = create_labeled_angle(90, "Right", "= 90°", include_arc=False).move_to(DOWN * 0.5)
        obtuse = create_labeled_angle(135, "Obtuse", "> 90°").move_to(RIGHT * 4 + DOWN * 0.5)

        # 3. Animations
        # Acute (has arc at index 2)
        self.play(Create(acute[0]), Create(acute[1]))
        self.play(Create(acute[2]), Write(acute[3]), Write(acute[4]))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Right (no arc, we add RightAngle symbol manually)
        self.play(Create(right[0]), Create(right[1]))
        right_symbol = RightAngle(right[0], right[1], length=0.3, color=YELLOW)
        # Note: right[2] and [3] are labels for 'right' group
        self.play(Create(right_symbol), Write(right[2]), Write(right[3]))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Obtuse (has arc at index 2)
        self.play(Create(obtuse[0]), Create(obtuse[1]))
        self.play(Create(obtuse[2]), Write(obtuse[3]), Write(obtuse[4]))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Final Highlight
        # Indicate the whole group including labels and the manual right_symbol
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(acute, right, obtuse, right_symbol)))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(acute, right, obtuse, right_symbol, title)))

from manim import *

class ConstantIntegral(Scene):

        # 1. Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=8,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        # 2. Define the constant function f(x) = 2

        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Shade the area from x=1 to x=4

        # 4. Integral Notation

            r"\int_1^4 2 \, dx = [2x]_1^4 = 8 - 2 = 6",

        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)

        self.wait(1)
        
        # Indicate the area and the result
        self.play(Indicate(area))
        self.play(Indicate(integral_tex[-1]))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class ProjectileMotion(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 8, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=10,
            y_length=6,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).add_coordinates().to_edge(DL, buff=0.5)
        
        # 2. Define the trajectory function: y = -0.25*(x-4)^2 + 4
        # Create the path first
        path = axes.plot(
            lambda x: -0.25 * (x - 4)**2 + 4,
            x_range=[0, 8],
            color=YELLOW
        )
        # Wrap it in DashedVMobject for the dashed effect
        trajectory = DashedVMobject(path, num_dashes=30).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)

        # 3. Ball object
        ball = Dot(color=RED).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        # 4. Title and Labels

        label = MathTex(r"y = v_0 t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).next_to(title, DOWN)

        self.add(axes, title, label)
        # Note: Create() works on DashedVMobject too
        self.play(Create(trajectory), run_time=2)
        
        # 5. Animate ball along the original path (smoother than animating along dashes)
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(ball, path),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class FactorsOfTwelve(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Center Number
        title = Text("Factors of 12", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        center_num = Text("12", font_size=72, color=YELLOW).center()
        self.add(title)
        self.play(Write(center_num))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 2. Define Factor Pairs
        pairs = [(1, 12), (2, 6), (3, 4)]
        colors = [GREEN, ORANGE, PURPLE]
        
        factor_mobs = VGroup()
        lines = VGroup()

        for i, (f1, f2) in enumerate(pairs):
            # Create factor texts
            t1 = Text(str(f1), font_size=40, color=colors[i])
            t2 = Text(str(f2), font_size=40, color=colors[i])
            
            # Position them symmetrically around the center
            # Pair 0: Left/Right, Pair 1: UL/DR, Pair 2: UR/DL
            angle = i * (PI / 3)
            dist = 2.5
            t1.move_to(center_num.get_center() + np.array([-np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * dist)
            t2.move_to(center_num.get_center() + np.array([np.cos(angle), -np.sin(angle), 0]) * dist)
            
            # Create connecting lines
            l1 = Line(center_num.get_center(), t1.get_center(), color=colors[i], stroke_opacity=0.5)
            l2 = Line(center_num.get_center(), t2.get_center(), color=colors[i], stroke_opacity=0.5)
            
            self.play(
                Create(l1), Create(l2),
                FadeIn(t1, shift=t1.get_center()-center_num.get_center()),
                FadeIn(t2, shift=t2.get_center()-center_num.get_center()),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            factor_mobs.add(t1, t2)
            lines.add(l1, l2)
            self.wait(0.3)

        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Final List of Factors
        all_factors = [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12]

Draw a secant line connecting (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)). Then, animate a tangent line moving along the curve to find a point 'c' where the tangent is parallel to the secant line, illustrating the theorem's core principle.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class MeanValueTheorem(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Axes and Function
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        def func(x): return 0.1 * x**3 - x
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=BLUE)
        
        title = Text("Mean Value Theorem", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(axes, graph, title)

        # 2. Define Points a and b
        a, b = -3, 2
        p_a = axes.c2p(a, func(a))
        p_b = axes.c2p(b, func(b))
        
        dot_a = Dot(p_a, color=YELLOW)
        dot_b = Dot(p_b, color=YELLOW)
        label_a = MathTex("a", font_size=24).next_to(p_a, DOWN)
        label_b = MathTex("b", font_size=24).next_to(p_b, DOWN)

        self.play(Create(dot_a), Create(dot_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))

        # 3. Secant Line
        secant_line = Line(p_a, p_b, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Tangent Line Animation
        # Derivative f'(x) = 0.3x^2 - 1
        # Target slope: (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)
        target_slope = (func(b) - func(a)) / (b - a)
        
        # Point c where f'(c) = target_slope
        # 0.3c^2 - 1 = target_slope
        c = np.sqrt((target_slope + 1) / 0.3) # We use the positive root for visualization
        p_c = axes.c2p(c, func(c))

        # Helper to create a tangent line at x
        def get_tangent_line(x):
            slope = 0.3 * x**2 - 1
            point = axes.c2p(x, func(x))
            # Create a line with the calculated slope
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED, stroke_width=3).scale(1.5)
            angle = np.arctan(slope)
            line.rotate(angle).move_to(point)
            return line

        # Animate tangent moving from a to b
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(a)
        tangent = always_redraw(lambda: get_tangent_line(x_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.add(tangent)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(c), run_time=3, rate_func=smooth)
        
        # Highlight the parallel state
        dot_c = Dot(p_c, color=RED)
        label_c = MathTex("c", color=RED, font_size=24).next_to(p_c, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(dot_c), Write(label_c))
        self.play(Indicate(tangent), Indicate(secant_line))
        
        explanation = MathTex("f'(c) = \\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}", font_size=32).to_corner(DL, buff=1.0)
        self.play(Write(explanation))
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class SpotlightReveal(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Background and Text
        self.camera.background_color = BLACK
        
        # Create text with very low opacity to be 'hidden'
        text_str = "HIDDEN KNOWLEDGE"
        hidden_text = Text(text_str, font_size=72, color=GREY_E, fill_opacity=0.1).center()
        
        # Create a bright version for the reveal effect
        # We'll use individual characters to handle specific highlights
        revealed_text = Text(text_str, font_size=72, color=WHITE).center()
        
        self.add(hidden_text)
        
        # 2. Setup Spotlight (The Tracker)
        spotlight = Circle(radius=1.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=2)
        spotlight.move_to(LEFT * 6) # Start off-screen left

        # 3. Redraw Logic for Highlighting
        # This is the 'Medium' complexity part: dynamically updating letter states
        # based on their distance to the moving spotlight.
        def update_letters(mobjects):
            spot_pos = spotlight.get_center()
            for i, char in enumerate(mobjects):
                # Calculate distance between spotlight center and character center
                dist = np.linalg.norm(char.get_center() - spot_pos)
                
                if dist < 1.2:
                    # Inside spotlight: Bright and slightly larger
                    # We interpolate opacity and scale for a smooth 'beam' feel
                    factor = inverse_interpolate(1.2, 0, dist)
                    char.set_color(interpolate_color(GREY_E, WHITE, factor))
                    char.set_fill(opacity=interpolate(0.1, 1.0, factor))
                else:
                    # Outside spotlight: Dim
                    char.set_color(GREY_E)
                    char.set_fill(opacity=0.1)

        revealed_text.add_updater(update_letters)
        self.add(revealed_text, spotlight)

        # 4. Animation
        title = Text("Typography: Spotlight Reveal", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Move the spotlight across the text
        self.play(
            spotlight.animate.move_to(RIGHT * 6),
            run_time=5,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # Final reveal: Fade the whole text in bright white
        revealed_text.remove_updater(update_letters)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(spotlight),
            revealed_text.animate.set_color(WHITE).set_fill(opacity=1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(revealed_text))
        self.wait(2)

class CollatzConjecture(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Collatz Conjecture (Start = 6)", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define the sequence
        sequence = [6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1]

            text = Text(str(val), font_size=24)
            nodes.add(VGroup(circle, text))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class CentripetalForce(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Circle
        title = Text("Uniform Circular Motion", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        circle = Circle(radius=2.5, color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        self.add(title, circle)

        # 2. State Tracking (Angle)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        radius = 2.5

        # 3. Dynamic Particle
        particle = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            circle.point_at_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()),
            color=BLUE, radius=0.12
        ))

        # 4. Dynamic Vectors
        # Velocity vector (Tangential)
        def get_velocity_vector():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            pos = circle.point_at_angle(theta)
            # Direction is (-sin(theta), cos(theta))
            direction = np.array([-np.sin(theta), np.cos(theta), 0])
            return Arrow(pos, pos + direction * 1.5, color=GREEN, buff=0, tip_length=0.2)

        # Acceleration vector (Centripetal)
        def get_acceleration_vector():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            pos = circle.point_at_angle(theta)
            # Direction is (-cos(theta), -sin(theta)) - towards ORIGIN
            return Arrow(pos, pos * 0.4, color=RED, buff=0, tip_length=0.2)

        velocity_vec = always_redraw(get_velocity_vector)
        acceleration_vec = always_redraw(get_acceleration_vector)

        # 5. Labels
        v_label = always_redraw(lambda: 
            MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=GREEN, font_size=32)
            .next_to(velocity_vec.get_end(), RIGHT if np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()) > 0 else LEFT, buff=0.1)
        )
        a_label = always_redraw(lambda: 
            MathTex(r"\vec{a}_c", color=RED, font_size=32)
            .next_to(acceleration_vec.get_center(), UP if np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()) < 0 else DOWN, buff=0.1)
        )

        self.add(particle, velocity_vec, acceleration_vec, v_label, a_label)

        # 6. Formula
        formula = MathTex(
            r"a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}",
            font_size=40,
            color=WHITE
        ).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0).add_background_rectangle()

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 7. Animation
        # Rotate 2 full laps (4*PI)
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI),
            run_time=8,
            rate_func=linear
        )

        self.wait(2)

        container = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*1.2 + UP*2, LEFT*1.2 + DOWN*2),
            Line(LEFT*1.2 + DOWN*2, RIGHT*1.2 + DOWN*2),
            Line(RIGHT*1.2 + DOWN*2, RIGHT*1.2 + UP*2)
        ).set_stroke(WHITE, width=4).move_to(DOWN*0.5)

        self.add(title, container)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 2. Helper to create a stack element
        def create_node(val):
            rect = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=2.0, height=0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6)
            text = Text(str(val), font_size=32)
            return VGroup(rect, text)

        stack_elements = []

        # 3. PUSH 10
        push_label = Text("PUSH 10", color=GREEN, font_size=28).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0)
        self.play(Write(push_label))
        
        node10 = create_node(10).move_to(LEFT * 5 + UP * 2)
        self.play(FadeIn(node10))
        # Move to bottom of container
        self.play(node10.animate.move_to(container.get_bottom() + UP * 0.45), run_time=1.5)
        stack_elements.append(node10)
        self.play(FadeOut(push_label))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 4. PUSH 20
        push_label = Text("PUSH 20", color=GREEN, font_size=28).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0)
        self.play(Write(push_label))
        
        node20 = create_node(20).move_to(LEFT * 5 + UP * 2)
        self.play(FadeIn(node20))
        # Move to top of node10
        self.play(node20.animate.move_to(node10.get_center() + UP * 0.85), run_time=1.5)
        stack_elements.append(node20)
        
        # Update 'Top' pointer
        top_pointer = Arrow(RIGHT * 2.5 + node20.get_y() * UP, node20.get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, color=YELLOW)
        top_label = Text("TOP", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).next_to(top_pointer, RIGHT)
        self.play(Create(top_pointer), Write(top_label))
        
        self.play(FadeOut(push_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. POP
        pop_label = Text("POP", color=RED, font_size=28).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0)
        self.play(Write(pop_label))
        
        # Remove the top element (20)
        target_pop = stack_elements.pop()
        
        # Animate top pointer moving down to node 10
        self.play(
            target_pop.animate.shift(UP * 2 + RIGHT * 4).set_opacity(0),
            top_pointer.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.85),
            top_label.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.85),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.remove(target_pop)
        self.play(FadeOut(pop_label))
        
        # 6. Final Indication
        self.play(Indicate(node10), Indicate(top_label))
        self.wait(2)

examples.instruction: Visualize the relationship between Sine and Cosine functions. Display a Unit Circle on the left. As a point moves around the circle, simultaneously trace two graphs on the right: one for sin(θ) in Blue and one for cos(θ) in Red. This clearly demonstrates the 90-degree phase shift between the two fundamental trigonometric functions.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class SineCosineTracer(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        # Left side for Circle, Right side for Graphs
        circle_origin = LEFT * 3.5
        axes_sine = Axes(
            x_range=[0, TAU, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1.5)

        axes_cosine = Axes(
            x_range=[0, TAU, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 1.5)

        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE).move_to(circle_origin)
        title = Text("Sine vs Cosine Relationship", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        
        self.add(circle, axes_sine, axes_cosine, title)

        # 2. Dynamic State via ValueTracker
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Rotating point and radius
        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            circle.point_at_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()),
            color=YELLOW
        ))
        radius = always_redraw(lambda: Line(circle_origin, dot.get_center(), color=YELLOW, stroke_opacity=0.5))

        # 3. Tracing Sine
        sine_dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes_sine.c2p(angle_tracker.get_value(), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())),
            color=BLUE
        ))
        sine_path = TracedPath(sine_dot.get_center, stroke_color=BLUE, stroke_width=4)
        sine_label = MathTex(r"\sin(\theta)", color=BLUE, font_size=24).next_to(axes_sine, UP, buff=0.1)

        # 4. Tracing Cosine
        cosine_dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes_cosine.c2p(angle_tracker.get_value(), np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value())),
            color=RED
        ))
        cosine_path = TracedPath(cosine_dot.get_center, stroke_color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        cosine_label = MathTex(r"\cos(\theta)", color=RED, font_size=24).next_to(axes_cosine, UP, buff=0.1)

        # 5. Connection Lines (Vertical and Horizontal projections)
        # Sine connection: from circle point to sine graph point (sharing y)
        sine_conn = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            dot.get_center(), 
            [axes_sine.c2p(0, np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()))[0] - 0.2, dot.get_y(), 0],
            color=BLUE, stroke_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2
        ))

        self.add(radius, dot, sine_dot, sine_path, sine_label, cosine_dot, cosine_path, cosine_label, sine_conn)

        # 6. Animation
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(TAU),
            run_time=10,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

examples.instruction: Visualize the composition of two linear transformations. Start with a unit square on a coordinate plane. First, apply a 45-degree rotation matrix (Matrix A). Then, apply a horizontal shear matrix (Matrix B) to the already rotated square. Finally, display the product matrix C = B * A and demonstrate that this single matrix represents the combined transformation.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class MatrixComposition(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Plane and Unit Square
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 5, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        unit_square = Square(side_length=1.0, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        unit_square.move_to(plane.c2p(0.5, 0.5))
        
        title = Text("Matrix Composition: B ⋅ A", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(plane, unit_square, title)

        # 2. Matrix A: Rotation (45 degrees)
        angle = 45 * DEGREES
        mat_a = [[np.cos(angle), -np.sin(angle)], [np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle)]]
        label_a = Text("Step 1: Rotation (A)", font_size=24, color=GREEN).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(label_a))
        self.play(
            unit_square.animate.apply_matrix(mat_a),
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(mat_a),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Matrix B: Horizontal Shear
        mat_b = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        label_b = Text("Step 2: Shear (B)", font_size=24, color=ORANGE).move_to(label_a).align_to(label_a, LEFT)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(label_a, label_b))
        self.play(
            unit_square.animate.apply_matrix(mat_b),
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(mat_b),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Show Combined Matrix C = B * A
        # Calculation for display
        combined_tex = MathTex(
            r"C = B \cdot A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 0.7 & -0.7 \\ 0.7 & 0.7 \end{bmatrix}",
            font_size=32
        ).to_corner(UR, buff=0.5).add_background_rectangle()
        
        result_tex = MathTex(
            r"C \approx \begin{bmatrix} 1.4 & 0 \\ 0.7 & 0.7 \end{bmatrix}",
            font_size=32, color=YELLOW
        ).next_to(combined_tex, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).add_background_rectangle()

        self.play(Write(combined_tex))
        self.play(FadeIn(result_tex, shift=UP))
        
        self.play(Indicate(unit_square), Indicate(result_tex))
        self.wait(2)

examples.instruction: Visualize the 'Partition' step of Quick Sort using the Lomuto scheme. Display an array [4, 2, 7, 1, 3] with the last element (3) as the pivot. Animate two pointers ('i' and 'j') moving through the array, swapping elements smaller than the pivot to the left side, and finally swapping the pivot into its correct sorted position.

from manim import *

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class QuickSortPartition(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Array
        title = Text("Quick Sort: Partition Step", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        values = [4, 2, 7, 1, 3]
        def create_array(vals):
            return VGroup(*[
                VGroup(
                    Square(side_length=0.9, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1),
                    Text(str(v), font_size=32)
                ) for v in vals
            ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).center()

        array_mobs = create_array(values)
        self.play(FadeIn(array_mobs))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 2. Identify Pivot (Last element)
        pivot_val = values[-1]
        pivot_rect = array_mobs[-1][0]
        pivot_label = Text("Pivot", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(pivot_rect, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(pivot_rect.animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=6).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.3), Write(pivot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Setup Pointers i and j
        # i tracks the boundary of smaller elements
        # j iterates through the array
        i_arrow = Arrow(DOWN * 0.8, ORIGIN, color=RED).scale(0.7).next_to(array_mobs[0], DOWN, buff=0.1).shift(LEFT * 1.1)
        i_label = Text("i", font_size=24, color=RED).next_to(i_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        j_arrow = Arrow(UP * 0.8, ORIGIN, color=GREEN).scale(0.7).next_to(array_mobs[0], UP, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", font_size=24, color=GREEN).next_to(j_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(i_arrow), Write(i_label), FadeIn(j_arrow), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Partition Loop Simulation
        # Values: [4, 2, 7, 1] vs Pivot 3
        
        # Step 1: j at 0 (val 4 > 3). No swap.
        self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[0][1]))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 2: j move to 1 (val 2 < 3). Swap with i+1.
        self.play(j_arrow.animate.next_to(array_mobs[1], UP), j_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[1], UP, buff=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[1][1], color=GREEN))
        
        # Move i to index 0 and swap array[0] with array[1]
        self.play(i_arrow.animate.next_to(array_mobs[0], DOWN), i_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[0], DOWN, buff=0.5))
        self.play(
            array_mobs[0].animate.move_to(array_mobs[1].get_center()),
            array_mobs[1].animate.move_to(array_mobs[0].get_center()),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        # Update internal VGroup references for further animations
        array_mobs[0], array_mobs[1] = array_mobs[1], array_mobs[0]
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 3: j move to 2 (val 7 > 3). No swap.
        self.play(j_arrow.animate.next_to(array_mobs[2], UP), j_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[2], UP, buff=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[2][1]))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 4: j move to 3 (val 1 < 3). Swap with i+1 (index 1).
        self.play(j_arrow.animate.next_to(array_mobs[3], UP), j_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[3], UP, buff=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[3][1], color=GREEN))
        
        # Move i to index 1 and swap array[1] with array[3]
        self.play(i_arrow.animate.next_to(array_mobs[1], DOWN), i_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[1], DOWN, buff=0.5))
        self.play(
            array_mobs[1].animate.move_to(array_mobs[3].get_center()),
            array_mobs[3].animate.move_to(array_mobs[1].get_center()),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        array_mobs[1], array_mobs[3] = array_mobs[3], array_mobs[1]
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 5. Final Pivot Swap: swap pivot with i+1 (index 2)
        final_msg = Text("Swap Pivot to Position i+1", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.0)
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        
        self.play(FadeOut(j_arrow), FadeOut(j_label))
        self.play(i_arrow.animate.next_to(array_mobs[2], DOWN), i_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[2], DOWN, buff=0.5))
        
        self.play(
            array_mobs[2].animate.move_to(array_mobs[4].get_center()),
            array_mobs[4].animate.move_to(array_mobs[2].get_center()),
            pivot_label.animate.next_to(array_mobs[2], UP, buff=1.2).shift(LEFT * 1.8), # adjust label pos
            run_time=2
        )
        array_mobs[2], array_mobs[4] = array_mobs[4], array_mobs[2]

        # 6. Success Highlight
        self.play(
            array_mobs[2][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(GREEN, width=6),
            FadeOut(final_msg),
            FadeOut(i_arrow), FadeOut(i_label)
        )
        res_label = Text("Pivot is in sorted position!", font_size=28, color=GREEN).to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.0)
        self.play(Write(res_label))
        self.wait(2)

Animate the process by maintaining a 'Queue' at the bottom. from manim import *

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class BFSVisualization(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Spacious Tree Layout
        title = Text("Breadth-First Search (BFS)", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(title)

        # Spacious node positions to prevent overlap
        # Level 0: y=2.2, Level 1: y=0.5, Level 2: y=-1.2
        node_pos = {
            0: [0, 2.2, 0],   # Root
            1: [-2.5, 0.5, 0], # Level 1 Left
            2: [2.5, 0.5, 0],  # Level 1 Right
            3: [-3.5, -1.2, 0], # Level 2 Left
            4: [1.5, -1.2, 0]   # Level 2 Right
        }

        nodes = {}
        for i, pos in node_pos.items():
            circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2)
            label = Text(str(i), font_size=24)
            nodes[i] = VGroup(circle, label).move_to(pos)

        # Create edges with proper buff to avoid touching node centers
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_bottom(), nodes[1].get_top(), buff=0.1),
            Line(nodes[0].get_bottom(), nodes[2].get_top(), buff=0.1),
            Line(nodes[1].get_bottom(), nodes[3].get_top(), buff=0.1),
            Line(nodes[2].get_bottom(), nodes[4].get_top(), buff=0.1)
        ).set_stroke(GREY, width=2)

        self.play(Create(edges), LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(nodes[i]) for i in nodes], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 2. Setup Queue Visualization at the bottom
        queue_box = Rectangle(width=6, height=1.2, color=WHITE).to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        queue_label = Text("Queue", font_size=24, color=GREY_A).next_to(queue_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(queue_box, queue_label)

        queue_mobs = VGroup()

        def update_queue():
            if len(queue_mobs) > 0:
                queue_mobs.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4).move_to(queue_box.get_center())

        # 3. BFS Animation Logic
        # Step 1: Start with root 0
        node0_q = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3), Text("0", font_size=24))
        queue_mobs.add(node0_q)
        update_queue()
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(node0_q, shift=UP),
            nodes[0][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Dequeue 0, Enqueue 1, 2
        self.play(
            nodes[0][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(GREEN, width=4),
            FadeOut(node0_q, scale=0.5),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        queue_mobs.remove(node0_q)

        # Create Enqueue elements
        node1_q = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3), Text("1", font_size=24))
        node2_q = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3), Text("2", font_size=24))
        queue_mobs.add(node1_q, node2_q)
        update_queue()
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(node1_q, shift=UP), 
            FadeIn(node2_q, shift=UP), 
            nodes[1][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=8),
            nodes[2][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Dequeue 1, Enqueue 3
        self.play(
            nodes[1][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(GREEN, width=4),
            FadeOut(node1_q, scale=0.5),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        queue_mobs.remove(node1_q)
        
        node3_q = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3), Text("3", font_size=24))
        queue_mobs.add(node3_q)
        update_queue() # This will slide node 2 to the left and node 3 next to it
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(node3_q, shift=UP),
            nodes[3][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=8),
            node2_q.animate.move_to(queue_mobs[0].get_center()) # Manual shift for clarity
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Dequeue 2, Enqueue 4
        self.play(
            nodes[2][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(GREEN, width=4),
            FadeOut(node2_q, scale=0.5),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        queue_mobs.remove(node2_q)

        node4_q = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3), Text("4", font_size=24))
        queue_mobs.add(node4_q)
        update_queue()

        self.play(
            FadeIn(node4_q, shift=UP),
            nodes[4][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=8),
            node3_q.animate.move_to(queue_mobs[0].get_center())
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Final Visit leaf nodes
        self.play(
            *[nodes[i][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(GREEN, width=4) for i in [3, 4]],
            FadeOut(queue_mobs),
            FadeOut(queue_box), FadeOut(queue_label)
        )
        
        success_text = Text("BFS Complete!", font_size=36, color=GREEN).move_to(DOWN * 2.5)
        self.play(Write(success_text))
        self.wait(2)

Animate a pointer starting at 0 and moving clockwise. As the pointer completes full circles, show a separate linear counter increasing (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ...) and display the corresponding congruence statement, e.g., '7 ≡ 2 (mod 5)', highlighting the remainder.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class ModularArithmeticClock(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Modular Arithmetic: Mod 5", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Create the Clock (Mod 5)
        mod_n = 5
        radius = 2.0
        clock_circle = Circle(radius=radius, color=WHITE)
        
        # Create numbers 0-4 around the circle
        # 0 at the top (90 deg), then clockwise
        labels = VGroup()
        for i in range(mod_n):
            angle = PI/2 - i * (TAU / mod_n)
            pos = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * radius
            num = Text(str(i), font_size=32).move_to(pos * 1.2)
            labels.add(num)

        self.add(clock_circle, labels)

        # 3. Pointer and Value Trackers
        # tracker counts the 'linear' number (0, 1, 2, 3...)
        val_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Hand/Pointer points to the current mod value
        # current_angle = 90deg - (val % 5) * (360/5)
        pointer = always_redraw(lambda: 
            Arrow(
                ORIGIN, 
                np.array([
                    np.cos(PI/2 - (val_tracker.get_value() % mod_n) * (TAU / mod_n)), 
                    np.sin(PI/2 - (val_tracker.get_value() % mod_n) * (TAU / mod_n)), 
                    0
                ]) * (radius - 0.2), 
                color=YELLOW, buff=0, tip_length=0.2
            )
        )

        # 4. Math Equation Display
        # n ≡ r (mod 5)
        eqn = always_redraw(lambda: 
            MathTex(
                f"{int(val_tracker.get_value())}", "\\equiv", 
                f"{int(val_tracker.get_value()) % mod_n}", 
                "\\pmod{5}",
                font_size=48
            ).to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.0)
        )
        # Color the remainder part
        # Note: MathTex index 0=n, 1=≡, 2=r, 3=(mod 5)
        def color_eqn(m):
            m[2].set_color(YELLOW)
            return m

        self.add(pointer, eqn)

        # 5. Animation

        self.play(
            val_tracker.animate.set_value(7),
            run_time=7,

        self.play(Indicate(labels[2], color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.5))

examples.instruction: Visualize the Nine-Point Circle theorem for an acute triangle ABC. Display the triangle and identify three sets of points: the midpoints of the sides, the feet of the altitudes, and the midpoints of the segments connecting the vertices to the orthocenter. Animate a single circle passing through all nine points simultaneously, demonstrating this remarkable geometric property.
examples.output:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class NinePointCircle(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("The Nine-Point Circle", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define Triangle ABC (Centered and scaled for frame safety)
        A = np.array([-1.5, 2.0, 0])
        B = np.array([2.5, -1.5, 0])
        C = np.array([-2.5, -1.5, 0])
        
        tri = Polygon(A, B, C, color=WHITE, stroke_width=3)
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("A", font_size=20).next_to(A, UP),
            Text("B", font_size=20).next_to(B, DR),
            Text("C", font_size=20).next_to(C, DL)
        )
        self.play(Create(tri), Write(labels))

        # 3. Calculate Key Points
        # Midpoints of sides
        M_ab = (A + B) / 2
        M_bc = (B + C) / 2
        M_ca = (C + A) / 2

        # Orthocenter H
        # Altitude from A: perpendicular to BC (horizontal line y=-1.5) -> vertical line x=-1.5
        # Altitude from B: perpendicular to AC
        slope_ac = (A[1] - C[1]) / (A[0] - C[0])
        perp_slope_ac = -1 / slope_ac
        # y - B[1] = perp_slope_ac * (x - B[0])
        # For A's altitude (x = -1.5):
        h_y = perp_slope_ac * (-1.5 - B[0]) + B[1]
        H = np.array([-1.5, h_y, 0])
        dot_h = Dot(H, color=RED, radius=0.06)
        label_h = Text("H", font_size=18, color=RED).next_to(H, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Altitudes (Feet)
        F_a = np.array([A[0], -1.5, 0]) # Foot from A to BC
        # Intersection of AC and altitude from B
        def get_intersect(p1, p2, p3, p4):
            x1,y1=p1[:2]; x2,y2=p2[:2]; x3,y3=p3[:2]; x4,y4=p4[:2]
            d = (y4-y3)*(x2-x1) - (x4-x3)*(y2-y1)
            ua = ((x4-x3)*(y1-y3) - (y4-y3)*(x1-x3)) / d
            return np.array([x1 + ua*(x2-x1), y1 + ua*(y2-y1), 0])
        
        F_b = get_intersect(A, C, B, H)
        F_c = get_intersect(A, B, C, H)

        # Euler Points (Midpoints of AH, BH, CH)
        E_a = (A + H) / 2
        E_b = (B + H) / 2
        E_c = (C + H) / 2

        # 4. Display Points in sets
        mid_dots = VGroup(Dot(M_ab), Dot(M_bc), Dot(M_ca)).set_color(YELLOW)
        alt_dots = VGroup(Dot(F_a), Dot(F_b), Dot(F_c)).set_color(ORANGE)
        eul_dots = VGroup(Dot(E_a), Dot(E_b), Dot(E_c)).set_color(PINK)

        self.play(FadeIn(dot_h), Write(label_h))
        self.play(FadeIn(mid_dots))
        self.play(FadeIn(alt_dots))
        self.play(FadeIn(eul_dots))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 5. The Nine-Point Circle
        # Center is midpoint of OH, but easier to calculate from 3 points (M_ab, M_bc, M_ca)
        # For an acute triangle, it's the circumcircle of the medial triangle
        # Center N is (Circumcenter + Orthocenter) / 2
        # Midpoint of BC is (0, -1.5). Perpendicular bisector is x=0.
        # AC slope was calculated. Perp bisector of AC through M_ca:
        m_ca_x, m_ca_y = M_ca[0], M_ca[1]
        # y - m_ca_y = perp_slope_ac * (x - m_ca_x)
        # Intersection with x=0:
        o_y = perp_slope_ac * (0 - m_ca_x) + m_ca_y
        O_center = np.array([0, o_y, 0]) # Circumcenter
        N_center = (O_center + H) / 2
        
        radius_n = np.linalg.norm(N_center - M_ab)
        nine_point_circle = Circle(radius=radius_n, color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=4).move_to(N_center)

        self.play(Create(nine_point_circle), run_time=3)
        self.play(Indicate(nine_point_circle))
        
        legend = VGroup(
            Text("● Midpoints", color=YELLOW, font_size=18),
            Text("● Altitude Feet", color=ORANGE, font_size=18),
            Text("● Euler Points", color=PINK, font_size=18)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).to_corner(DL, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(legend))
        self.wait(3)

examples.instruction: Visualize the chaotic motion of a Double Pendulum. Display two connected rods attached to a fixed pivot. Animate the pendulum swinging under gravity. Use a 'TracedPath' to draw the trajectory of the bottom mass in a bright color, illustrating how the motion becomes highly complex and non-repeating over time. Display the governing differential equations briefly at the start.
examples.output:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class DoublePendulum(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Double Pendulum: Chaotic Motion", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Physics Constants and Initial State
        L1, L2 = 2.0, 1.8  # Lengths of rods
        M1, M2 = 1.0, 1.0  # Masses
        G = 9.8            # Gravity
        
        # Initial angles (radians) and velocities
        theta1 = 120 * DEGREES
        theta2 = -10 * DEGREES
        omega1 = 0.0
        omega2 = 0.0
        
        state = np.array([theta1, omega1, theta2, omega2])

        # 3. Differential Equations (Numerical Integration)
        def get_derivatives(state, t):
            t1, w1, t2, w2 = state
            
            # Equation for t1 acceleration
            num1 = -G * (2 * M1 + M2) * np.sin(t1) - M2 * G * np.sin(t1 - 2 * t2) - 2 * np.sin(t1 - t2) * M2 * (w2**2 * L2 + w1**2 * L1 * np.cos(t1 - t2))
            den1 = L1 * (2 * M1 + M2 - M2 * np.cos(2 * t1 - 2 * t2))
            a1 = num1 / den1
            
            # Equation for t2 acceleration
            num2 = 2 * np.sin(t1 - t2) * (w1**2 * L1 * (M1 + M2) + G * (M1 + M2) * np.cos(t1) + w2**2 * L2 * M2 * np.cos(t1 - t2))
            den2 = L2 * (2 * M1 + M2 - M2 * np.cos(2 * t1 - 2 * t2))
            a2 = num2 / den2
            
            return np.array([w1, a1, w2, a2])

        # 4. Display Equations briefly
        eqs = MathTex(
            r"\ddot{\theta}_1 = f_1(\theta_1, \theta_2, \dot{\theta}_1, \dot{\theta}_2)",
            r"\ddot{\theta}_2 = f_2(\theta_1, \theta_2, \dot{\theta}_1, \dot{\theta}_2)",
            font_size=32
        ).to_corner(UL, buff=0.8).add_background_rectangle()
        self.play(Write(eqs))
        self.wait(1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(eqs))

        # 5. Visual Components
        pivot = Dot(UP * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.add(pivot)
        
        self.curr_state = state
        
        def update_pendulum(mobj, dt):
            sub_steps = 10
            h = dt / sub_steps
            for _ in range(sub_steps):
                k1 = get_derivatives(self.curr_state, 0)
                k2 = get_derivatives(self.curr_state + h/2 * k1, 0)
                k3 = get_derivatives(self.curr_state + h/2 * k2, 0)
                k4 = get_derivatives(self.curr_state + h * k3, 0)
                self.curr_state = self.curr_state + (h/6) * (k1 + 2*k2 + 2*k3 + k4)

            t1, _, t2, _ = self.curr_state
            p1 = pivot.get_center() + L1 * np.array([np.sin(t1), -np.cos(t1), 0])
            p2 = p1 + L2 * np.array([np.sin(t2), -np.cos(t2), 0])
            
            mobj[0].set_points_as_corners([pivot.get_center(), p1])
            mobj[1].set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
            mobj[2].move_to(p1)
            mobj[3].move_to(p2)

        rod1 = Line(pivot.get_center(), pivot.get_center() + DOWN * L1, color=GREY_A)
        rod2 = Line(rod1.get_end(), rod1.get_end() + DOWN * L2, color=GREY_A)
        mass1 = Dot(rod1.get_end(), radius=0.15, color=BLUE)
        mass2 = Dot(rod2.get_end(), radius=0.15, color=RED)
        
        pendulum = VGroup(rod1, rod2, mass1, mass2)
        pendulum.add_updater(update_pendulum)
        
        path = TracedPath(mass2.get_center, stroke_color=RED, stroke_width=2, dissipating_time=2.0)

        self.add(path, pendulum)

        # 6. Run Simulation
        self.wait(15)
        
        # Final Highlight
        pendulum.remove_updater(update_pendulum)
        self.play(Indicate(title))
        self.wait(2)

class AVLRotation(Scene):

        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("AVL Tree: Right-Left (RL) Rotation", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Helper for Nodes
        def create_node(label, pos):
            c = Circle(radius=0.35, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2).move_to(pos)
            t = Text(label, font_size=20).move_to(pos)
            return VGroup(c, t)

        # 3. Initial Unbalanced State Positions
        pos10 = UP * 0.5 + LEFT * 1.5
        pos30 = DOWN * 0.5 + RIGHT * 1.0
        pos20 = DOWN * 2.0 + LEFT * 0.5

        n10 = create_node("10", pos10)
        n30 = create_node("30", pos30)
        n20 = create_node("20", pos20)

        # CRITICAL FIX: Initialize tracking attributes BEFORE always_redraw calls
        self.e1_start, self.e1_end = n10, n30
        self.e2_start, self.e2_end = n30, n20

        # 4. Setup Dynamic Edges
        # Edges will automatically follow the centers of their assigned start/end nodes
        edge1 = always_redraw(lambda: Line(self.e1_start[0].get_center(), self.e1_end[0].get_center(), buff=0.35))
        edge2 = always_redraw(lambda: Line(self.e2_start[0].get_center(), self.e2_end[0].get_center(), buff=0.35))

        self.play(FadeIn(n10), FadeIn(n30), FadeIn(n20), Create(edge1), Create(edge2))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. STEP 1: Right Rotation on 30
        step1_label = Text("Step 1: Right Rotation on 30", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).to_corner(UL, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(step1_label))

        # Update logical connections: 10 -> 20, 20 -> 30
        self.e1_end = n20
        self.e2_start = n20
        self.e2_end = n30

        # New positions for nodes after Step 1
        new_pos30 = DOWN * 2.0 + RIGHT * 2.5
        new_pos20 = DOWN * 0.5 + RIGHT * 1.0

        self.play(
            n30.animate.move_to(new_pos30),
            n20.animate.move_to(new_pos20),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 6. STEP 2: Left Rotation on 10
        step2_label = Text("Step 2: Left Rotation on 10", font_size=20, color=GREEN).to_corner(UL, buff=0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(step1_label, step2_label))

        # Update logical connections: 20 is new root, 10 and 30 are children
        self.e1_start = n20
        self.e1_end = n10
        # e2 is already 20 -> 30

        # Final balanced positions
        final_pos20 = UP * 0.5
        final_pos10 = DOWN * 1.5 + LEFT * 2.5
        final_pos30 = DOWN * 1.5 + RIGHT * 2.5

        self.play(
            n20.animate.move_to(final_pos20),
            n10.animate.move_to(final_pos10),
            n30.animate.move_to(final_pos30),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(n20))
        success = Text("Tree is now balanced!", font_size=24, color=GREEN).to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(success))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class TextToInfinity(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Typography: Symbol Morphing", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Initial Text
        word = Text("INFINITY", font_size=72, weight=BOLD)
        word.set_color(WHITE)
        word.center()
        
        self.play(Write(word, run_time=2))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 3. Define the Lemniscate (Infinity Symbol) Path
        # x = a*cos(t) / (1 + sin^2(t)), y = a*sin(t)*cos(t) / (1 + sin^2(t))
        a_param = 3.5
        lemniscate = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                a_param * np.cos(t) / (1 + np.sin(t)**2),
                a_param * np.sin(t) * np.cos(t) / (1 + np.sin(t)**2),
                0
            ]),
            t_range=[0, TAU],
            color=RED,
            stroke_width=6
        ).shift(DOWN * 0.2)

        # 4. Transform Text to Symbol
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(word, lemniscate),
            run_time=3,

examples.instruction: Visualize the Fourier Series approximation of a Square Wave using rotating epicycles. Display a vertical axis on the left. Animate a series of four rotating vectors (harmonics 1, 3, 5, and 7) connected end-to-end. As they rotate at their respective frequencies, have the tip of the final vector trace a blue wave moving to the right, demonstrating how the summation of sine waves converges to a square shape.
examples.output:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class FourierSeriesSquare(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Fourier Series: Square Wave Approximation", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Axes
        # Left side for circles, Right side for tracing wave
        circle_origin = LEFT * 3.5
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=7, y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).shift(RIGHT * 2.5)
        
        self.add(axes)

        # 3. Fourier Constants (n = 1, 3, 5, 7)
        n_terms = [1, 3, 5, 7]
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # 4. Epicycle Logic
        def get_epicycles(t):
            points = [circle_origin]
            current_p = circle_origin
            for n in n_terms:
                # Radius for square wave harmonic: 4 / (n * PI)
                radius = (4 / (n * PI)) * 1.5 # 1.5 is a scaling factor for visibility
                angle = n * t
                new_p = current_p + radius * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
                points.append(new_p)
                current_p = new_p
            return points

        # Redrawer for circles and vectors
        circles_and_vectors = always_redraw(lambda:
            VGroup(*[
                VGroup(
                    Circle(radius=np.linalg.norm(pts[i+1] - pts[i]), color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.2),
                    Line(pts[i], pts[i+1], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2),
                    Dot(pts[i+1], radius=0.04, color=YELLOW)
                ).move_to(pts[i], aligned_edge=pts[i]-pts[i+1]) # This is tricky, easier to just use points
                for i, pts in [(i, get_epicycles(time_tracker.get_value())) for i in range(len(n_terms))]
            ])
        )
        
        # Simplified redrawer for vectors
        def create_visual_epicycles():
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            pts = get_epicycles(t)
            res = VGroup()
            for i in range(len(n_terms)):
                r = np.linalg.norm(pts[i+1] - pts[i])
                c = Circle(radius=r, color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.2).move_to(pts[i])
                l = Line(pts[i], pts[i+1], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
                res.add(c, l)
            return res

        visual_epicycles = always_redraw(create_visual_epicycles)

        # 5. Tracing the Wave
        # The dot at the tip of the last epicycle
        tip_dot = always_redraw(lambda:
            Dot(get_epicycles(time_tracker.get_value())[-1], color=RED, radius=0.08)
        )

        # Connection line from tip to the graph
        conn_line = always_redraw(lambda:
            Line(
                tip_dot.get_center(),
                axes.c2p(0, tip_dot.get_center()[1] - axes.c2p(0,0)[1]), # Local Y relative to graph
                color=RED, stroke_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=1
            )
        )
        # Correction: c2p uses absolute coords
        conn_line = always_redraw(lambda:
            Line(
                tip_dot.get_center(),
                [axes.c2p(0,0)[0], tip_dot.get_y(), 0],
                color=RED, stroke_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=1
            )
        )

        # TracedPath for the wave
        # We need the dot to move relative to the axes for a proper trace
        # or use a moving graph. Let's trace in world space and shift the graph?
        # Better: use a dot that stays at x=0 on axes and trace that.
        graph_dot = always_redraw(lambda:
            Dot(axes.c2p(0, tip_dot.get_y() - circle_origin[1]), color=RED, radius=0.01)
        )
        
        # To make the wave 'move' right, we actually trace the y and shift the path
        wave_path = TracedPath(graph_dot.get_center, stroke_color=BLUE, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Actually, let's just use the tip to trace a line and shift it manually or use a standard trick:
        # dot on graph moves right as time increases.
        moving_graph_dot = always_redraw(lambda:
            Dot(axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value() % 6, tip_dot.get_y() - circle_origin[1]), color=BLUE, radius=0.05)
        )
        wave_trace = TracedPath(moving_graph_dot.get_center, stroke_color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)

        self.add(visual_epicycles, tip_dot, conn_line, moving_graph_dot, wave_trace)

        # 6. Formula
        formula = MathTex(
            r"f(x) \approx \sum_{n=1,3,5,7} \frac{4}{n\pi} \sin(n\omega t)",
            font_size=32,
            color=WHITE
        ).to_corner(DL, buff=0.8).add_background_rectangle()
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # 7. Animation
        # Run for 2 full cycles of the fundamental
        self.play(
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(TAU * 2),
            run_time=12,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

            nodes[1].animate.move_to(node_pos[0]),

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup

class DFSBacktracking(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("DFS with Backtracking", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define Graph Structure
        # A -> [B, C], B -> [D, E]
        node_pos = {
            "A": UP * 1.5,
            "B": LEFT * 2 + DOWN * 0.5,
            "C": RIGHT * 2 + DOWN * 0.5,
            "D": LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 2.5,
            "E": LEFT * 1 + DOWN * 2.5
        }

        nodes = {}
        for name, pos in node_pos.items():
            nodes[name] = VGroup(
                Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2),
                Text(name, font_size=24)
            ).move_to(pos)

        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes["A"].get_bottom(), nodes["B"].get_top()),
            Line(nodes["A"].get_bottom(), nodes["C"].get_top()),
            Line(nodes["B"].get_bottom(), nodes["D"].get_top()),
            Line(nodes["B"].get_bottom(), nodes["E"].get_top())
        ).set_stroke(GREY, width=2)

        self.add(edges, *nodes.values())
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Stack Visualization (Right Side)
        stack_rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=3, color=WHITE).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        stack_label = Text("Recursion Stack", font_size=20).next_to(stack_rect, UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(stack_rect, stack_label)
        
        stack_contents = VGroup()

        def push_stack(name):
            label = Text(name, font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
            if len(stack_contents) == 0:
                label.move_to(stack_rect.get_bottom() + UP * 0.4)
            else:
                label.next_to(stack_contents[-1], UP, buff=0.2)
            stack_contents.add(label)
            return FadeIn(label, shift=UP)

        def pop_stack():
            target = stack_contents[-1]
            stack_contents.remove(target)
            return FadeOut(target, shift=DOWN)

        # 4. DFS Animation Steps
        # Step 1: Visit A
        self.play(nodes["A"][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5), push_stack("A"))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 2: Move to B
        self.play(
            nodes["B"][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5),
            push_stack("B"),
            edges[0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=4)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 3: Move to D (Dead End)
        self.play(
            nodes["D"][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5),
            push_stack("D"),
            edges[2].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=4)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 4: BACKTRACK from D
        backtrack_label = Text("Dead End! Backtracking...", font_size=20, color=RED).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(backtrack_label), nodes["D"][0].animate.set_stroke(RED, width=8))
        self.play(pop_stack(), edges[2].animate.set_stroke(GREY, width=2, opacity=0.3))
        self.play(FadeOut(backtrack_label), nodes["D"][0].animate.set_stroke(WHITE, width=2))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 5: Move to E
        self.play(
            nodes["E"][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5),
            push_stack("E"),
            edges[3].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=4)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 6: BACKTRACK from E and B
        self.play(pop_stack(), edges[3].animate.set_stroke(GREY, width=2, opacity=0.3))
        self.play(pop_stack(), edges[0].animate.set_stroke(GREY, width=2, opacity=0.3))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 7: Move to C
        self.play(
            nodes["C"][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5),
            push_stack("C"),
            edges[1].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=4)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Final State
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(*nodes.values())), color=GREEN)
        success = Text("DFS Traversal Complete", font_size=32, color=GREEN).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(success))
        self.wait(2)

Animate numbers 1 through 49 being placed in a counter-clockwise outward spiral. As each number is placed, highlight it in Blue if it is prime. This demonstrates the mysterious non-random patterns and diagonal alignments of prime numbers in a spiral arrangement.
examples.output:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup
config.no_latex_cleanup = True

class UlamSpiral(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Ulam Spiral (1 to 49)", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Helper to check for Primes
        def is_prime(n):
            if n < 2: return False
            for i in range(2, int(np.sqrt(n)) + 1):
                if n % i == 0: return False
            return True

        # 3. Spiral Path Generation
        # Directions: Right, Up, Left, Down
        directions = [RIGHT, UP, LEFT, DOWN]
        
        # Grid spacing
        step_size = 0.8
        current_pos = ORIGIN + DOWN * 0.5
        current_num = 1
        step_count = 1
        dir_idx = 0

        grid = VGroup()
        
        # 4. Animation Loop
        # We'll do 7x7 = 49 numbers
        while current_num <= 49:
            # For each 'lap' size, we move in two directions
            for _ in range(2):
                for _ in range(step_count):
                    if current_num > 49: break
                    
                    # Create cell
                    cell = Square(side_length=step_size, stroke_width=1, color=GREY_E)
                    cell.move_to(current_pos)
                    label = Text(str(current_num), font_size=18).move_to(current_pos)
                    
                    cell_group = VGroup(cell, label)
                    
                    # Check if prime and highlight
                    if is_prime(current_num):
                        cell.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.4)
                        cell.set_stroke(BLUE, width=3)
                        label.set_color(BLUE_A)
                        self.play(FadeIn(cell_group), run_time=0.2)
                    else:
                        self.play(FadeIn(cell_group), run_time=0.1)
                    
                    grid.add(cell_group)
                    
                    # Move to next position
                    current_pos += directions[dir_idx] * step_size
                    current_num += 1
                
                if current_num > 49: break
                # Rotate direction
                dir_idx = (dir_idx + 1) % 4
            
            # Increase steps per direction every two changes
            step_count += 1

        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Highlight Diagonal Patterns
        # Show diagonal lines to emphasize prime alignment
        diag_line = Line(grid[0].get_center(), grid[48].get_center(), color=YELLOW, stroke_opacity=0.3)
        self.play(Create(diag_line))
        
        pattern_text = Text("Emerging Diagonal Patterns", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(pattern_text))
        
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(*[g for i, g in enumerate(grid) if is_prime(i+1)])))
        self.wait(3)

# Windows-specific fix for PermissionError: [WinError 32] during LaTeX cleanup

class MonteCarloPi(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Monte Carlo: PI Estimation", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Geometry
        square = Square(side_length=3, color=WHITE)
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(square), Create(circle))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 3. State Tracking
        self.in_count = 0
        self.total_count = 0
        
        # 4. Manual Formula Construction (NO MathTex fractions to avoid errors)
        # We build the formula [ PI approx 4 * (Nin / Ntot) = ] using Text and VGroup
        f_pi = Text("PI", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        f_approx = Text(" ≈ 4 × ", font_size=24)
        
        # Fraction parts
        f_num = Text("Nin", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        f_line = Line(LEFT * 0.35, RIGHT * 0.35, stroke_width=2)
        f_den = Text("Ntot", font_size=20)
        f_frac = VGroup(f_num, f_line, f_den).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        f_equals = Text(" = ", font_size=24)
        
        formula = VGroup(f_pi, f_approx, f_frac, f_equals).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).to_corner(UR, buff=0.6)
        
        # Dynamic Pi value
        pi_display = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=4, color=YELLOW, font_size=28).next_to(formula, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Counters
        in_label = Integer(0, font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        tot_label = Integer(0, font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        stats = VGroup(
            Text("In: ", font_size=20, color=GREEN), in_label,
            Text(" Total: ", font_size=20, color=WHITE), tot_label
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).to_corner(UL, buff=0.6)
        
        self.add(stats, formula, pi_display)

        # 5. Simulation Logic
        def get_random_point():
            return np.array([random.uniform(-1.5, 1.5), random.uniform(-1.5, 1.5), 0])

        # Individual drops
        for _ in range(15):
            self.total_count += 1
            pos = get_random_point()
            is_inside = np.linalg.norm(pos) <= 1.5
            if is_inside: self.in_count += 1
            
            dot = Dot(pos, radius=0.04, color=GREEN if is_inside else RED)
            self.play(
                FadeIn(dot, scale=2),
                in_label.animate.set_value(self.in_count),
                tot_label.animate.set_value(self.total_count),
                pi_display.animate.set_value(4 * self.in_count / self.total_count),
                run_time=0.2
            )

        # Batch drops
        for _ in range(4):
            batch = VGroup()
            for _ in range(25):
                self.total_count += 1
                pos = get_random_point()
                is_inside = np.linalg.norm(pos) <= 1.5
                if is_inside: self.in_count += 1
                batch.add(Dot(pos, radius=0.03, color=GREEN if is_inside else RED))
            
            self.play(
                FadeIn(batch),
                in_label.animate.set_value(self.in_count),
                tot_label.animate.set_value(self.total_count),
                pi_display.animate.set_value(4 * self.in_count / self.total_count),
                run_time=0.4
            )

        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Indicate(pi_display))
        self.wait(2)

examples.instruction: Visualize the Sum Rule for derivatives in calculus. Show that the derivative of a sum of two functions, f(x) + g(x), is equal to the sum of their individual derivatives, f'(x) + g'(x). The animation should display the symbolic rule clearly, using distinct colors for each function to help the viewer track the transformation process.

from manim import *

class SumRuleDerivative(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Calculus: The Sum Rule", font_size=40).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Display the rule symbolically
        # d/dx [f(x) + g(x)] = f'(x) + g'(x)
        
        # Left side
        lhs = MathTex(
            "\\frac{d}{dx}", "[", "f(x)", "+", "g(x)", "]", 
            tex_to_color_map={"f(x)": BLUE, "g(x)": GREEN}
        ).scale(1.2).move_to(LEFT * 2)

        # Right side
        rhs = MathTex(
            "=", "f'(x)", "+", "g'(x)",
            tex_to_color_map={"f'(x)": BLUE, "g'(x)": GREEN}
        ).scale(1.2).next_to(lhs, RIGHT, buff=0.3)

        # 3. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(lhs))
        self.wait(1)

        # Distribute the derivative operator
        # Illustrate the 'flow' of d/dx to f(x) and g(x)
        self.play(Write(rhs[0])) # Write the '=' sign
        
        # Highlight the f(x) part being transformed
        self.play(
            Indicate(lhs[2], color=BLUE),
            Write(rhs[1]), # Write f'(x)
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Show the '+' sign
        self.play(Write(rhs[2]))

        # Highlight the g(x) part being transformed
        self.play(
            Indicate(lhs[4], color=GREEN),
            Write(rhs[3]), # Write g'(x)
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Conclusion box
        rule_box = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(lhs, rhs), color=YELLOW, buff=0.4)
        conclusion = Text("The derivative of a sum is the sum of the derivatives", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        conclusion.next_to(rule_box, DOWN, buff=0.5)

        self.play(Create(rule_box), FadeIn(conclusion, shift=UP))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, lhs, rhs, rule_box, conclusion)))

from manim import *

class NewtonsSecondLaw(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Formula
        title = Text("Newton's Second Law", font_size=40).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        formula = MathTex("F", "=", "m", "a", font_size=48).next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("F", RED)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("a", BLUE)
        
        self.add(title, formula)

        # 2. Setup Block and Ground
        ground = Line(LEFT * 5, RIGHT * 5, color=GREY).shift(DOWN * 1.5)
        block = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).next_to(ground, UP, buff=0)
        mass_label = Text("m = 1kg", font_size=24).move_to(block.get_center())
        
        self.add(ground, block, mass_label)

        # 3. Force and Acceleration Vectors (using ValueTracker for dynamic scaling)
        # We'll simulate two scenarios: Small Force vs Large Force
        force_val = ValueTracker(1)
        
        # Force vector (Pushing from the left)
        force_vec = always_redraw(lambda: Arrow(
            start=block.get_left() + LEFT * (force_val.get_value() * 1.2), # Increased base length
            end=block.get_left(),
            color=RED, buff=0, stroke_width=6
        ))
        # Position label relative to the vector but shifted left to clear the block
        force_label = always_redraw(lambda: Text("Force (F)", font_size=18, color=RED)
            .next_to(force_vec, UP, buff=0.2)
            .align_to(force_vec, LEFT))

        # Acceleration vector (Resultant)
        accel_vec = always_redraw(lambda: Arrow(
            start=block.get_right(),
            end=block.get_right() + RIGHT * (force_val.get_value() * 0.8),
            color=BLUE, buff=0, stroke_width=4
        ))
        # Position label relative to the vector but shifted right to clear the block
        accel_label = always_redraw(lambda: Text("Accel (a)", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
            .next_to(accel_vec, UP, buff=0.2)
            .align_to(accel_vec, RIGHT))

        self.play(Create(force_vec), Write(force_label))
        self.play(Create(accel_vec), Write(accel_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Animation: Scenario 1 (Small Force)
        # Move the block slowly to represent low acceleration
        self.play(
            block.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1),
            mass_label.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Animation: Scenario 2 (Increase Force -> Increase Acceleration)
        # Increase the force tracker, then move the block faster
        self.play(
            force_val.animate.set_value(3),
            formula[3].animate.scale(1.5).set_color(YELLOW), # Emphasize 'a' in formula
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(
            block.animate.shift(RIGHT * 3),
            mass_label.animate.shift(RIGHT * 3),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=rush_from
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, formula, ground, block, mass_label, force_vec, force_label, accel_vec, accel_label)))

class SohCahToa(Scene):

from manim import *

class CountingSortPhase(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Counting Sort: The Counting Phase", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define Input Array
        input_values = [1, 0, 3, 1, 2, 1]
        input_mobs = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                Square(side_length=0.7, color=BLUE_D, fill_opacity=0.3),
                Text(str(v), font_size=24)
            ) for v in input_values
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).center().shift(UP * 1.0)
        
        input_label = Text("Input Array", font_size=20, color=GREY_A).next_to(input_mobs, UP, buff=0.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(input_mobs), Write(input_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Define Counting Array (Frequency Array)
        # Max value is 3, so we need 4 slots (0, 1, 2, 3)
        count_values = [0, 0, 0, 0]
        count_mobs = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                Square(side_length=0.9, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1),
                Text(str(v), font_size=30, color=YELLOW) # This is the counter
            ) for v in count_values
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).center().shift(DOWN * 1.5)

        # Add index labels for counting array
        count_indices = VGroup(*[
            Text(str(i), font_size=18, color=GREY_A).next_to(count_mobs[i], DOWN, buff=0.1)
            for i in range(4)
        ])

        count_label = Text("Counting (Frequency) Array", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(count_mobs, UP, buff=0.2)

        self.play(Create(count_mobs), FadeIn(count_indices), Write(count_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Counting Process Animation
        for i, val in enumerate(input_values):
            # Highlight the input element
            self.play(Indicate(input_mobs[i], color=YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Create a ghost of the value to move
            ghost_val = Text(str(val), font_size=24, color=YELLOW).move_to(input_mobs[i].get_center())

            )

            )
            self.play(Indicate(count_mobs[val][0], color=GREEN), run_time=0.4)
            self.wait(0.2)

examples.instruction: Visualize the algorithm to find the maximum value in an unsorted array. Display an array of six integers: [14, 25, 8, 42, 17, 33]. Animate a pointer moving through the array from left to right. Maintain a 'Current Max' label that updates whenever a larger number is encountered, highlighting the new maximum in Green and smaller numbers in Red during the comparison.
examples.output:
from manim import *

class FindMaxValue(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Algorithm: Find Maximum Value", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define Unsorted Array
        values = [14, 25, 8, 42, 17, 33]
        array_mobs = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                Square(side_length=0.9, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1),
                Text(str(v), font_size=28)
            ) for v in values
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).center()

        self.play(FadeIn(array_mobs))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Setup 'Current Max' Tracker
        max_val = values[0]
        max_label_text = Text("Current Max: ", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        max_val_mob = Text(str(max_val), font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        max_tracker_group = VGroup(max_label_text, max_val_mob).arrange(RIGHT).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0)

        self.play(Write(max_tracker_group))
        self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[0], color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 4. Search Loop
        pointer = Arrow(DOWN * 0.8, ORIGIN, color=YELLOW).scale(0.7)
        pointer.next_to(array_mobs[0], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(pointer))

        for i in range(1, len(values)):
            # Move pointer
            self.play(pointer.animate.next_to(array_mobs[i], DOWN, buff=0.1), run_time=0.6)
            
            # Comparison highlight
            curr_val = values[i]
            self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[i][0], color=WHITE), run_time=0.4)

            if curr_val > max_val:
                # New Max Found!
                old_max_val = max_val
                max_val = curr_val
                new_max_mob = Text(str(max_val), font_size=32, color=GREEN).move_to(max_val_mob.get_center())
                
                self.play(
                    array_mobs[i][0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.4).set_color(GREEN),
                    Transform(max_val_mob, new_max_mob),
                    # Reset previous max box if it was colored
                    *[array_mobs[j][0].animate.set_fill(opacity=0.1).set_color(WHITE) 
                      for j in range(i) if values[j] == old_max_val]
                )
                self.play(Indicate(max_val_mob, scale_factor=1.3))
            else:
                # Not a new max
                self.play(array_mobs[i][0].animate.set_color(RED), run_time=0.4)
                self.wait(0.2)
                self.play(array_mobs[i][0].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.2)

        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Final Result
        final_msg = Text(f"Maximum Value is {max_val}", font_size=32, color=GREEN).next_to(array_mobs, UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        self.play(Indicate(final_msg))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, array_mobs, max_tracker_group, pointer, final_msg)))
