from manim import *
import numpy as np

class LawOfReflection(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Physics: The Law of Reflection", font_size=40, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Mirror and Normal
        mirror = Line(LEFT * 4, RIGHT * 4, color=GREY_A, stroke_width=6)
        mirror.shift(DOWN * 1.5)
        mirror_label = Text("Mirror Surface", font_size=20, color=GREY_A).next_to(mirror, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        normal = DashedLine(mirror.get_center(), mirror.get_center() + UP * 4, color=WHITE)
        normal_label = Text("Normal", font_size=20).next_to(normal, UP, buff=0.2)

        self.play(Create(mirror), Write(mirror_label))
        self.play(Create(normal), Write(normal_label))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 3. Define Rays
        angle = 45 * DEGREES
        hit_point = mirror.get_center()
        
        # Incident Ray (Coming from top-left)
        start_point = hit_point + rotate_vector(UP * 3.5, angle)
        incident_ray = Arrow(start_point, hit_point, color=YELLOW, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        incident_label = Text("Incident Ray", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).next_to(start_point, LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Reflected Ray (Going to top-right)
        end_point = hit_point + rotate_vector(UP * 3.5, -angle)
        reflected_ray = Arrow(hit_point, end_point, color=ORANGE, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        reflected_label = Text("Reflected Ray", font_size=24, color=ORANGE).next_to(end_point, RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # 4. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(incident_ray), Write(incident_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show the reflected ray
        self.play(Create(reflected_ray), Write(reflected_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Label Angles
        # Using explicit Arc for more predictable results than Angle()
        # Incidence Angle (90 to 135 degrees)
        arc_i = Arc(start_angle=90*DEGREES, angle=45*DEGREES, radius=0.8, arc_center=hit_point, color=YELLOW)
        label_i = MathTex(r"\theta_i", color=YELLOW, font_size=32).move_to(
            hit_point + rotate_vector(UP * 1.2, 22.5 * DEGREES)
        )

        # Reflection Angle (45 to 90 degrees)
        # Note: Arc angle is always CCW, so we start at 45 and go +45 to 90
        arc_r = Arc(start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=45*DEGREES, radius=0.8, arc_center=hit_point, color=ORANGE)
        label_r = MathTex(r"\theta_r", color=ORANGE, font_size=32).move_to(
            hit_point + rotate_vector(UP * 1.2, -22.5 * DEGREES)
        )

        self.play(Create(arc_i), Write(label_i))
        self.play(Create(arc_r), Write(label_r))
        self.wait(1)

        # 6. Display the Law
        law_text = MathTex(r"\theta_i = \theta_r", font_size=48, color=YELLOW).to_corner(DR, buff=1)
        self.play(Write(law_text))
        self.play(Indicate(law_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, mirror, mirror_label, normal, normal_label, incident_ray, incident_label, reflected_ray, reflected_label, arc_i, label_i, arc_r, label_r, law_text)))

class StackPush(Scene):

        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Stack Container
        # A 3-sided rectangle (top open)
        stack_rect = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT * 1.5 + UP * 2, LEFT * 1.5 + DOWN * 2),

from manim import *

class GnomeSortVisual(Scene):

        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Gnome Sort (The 'Stupid' Sort)", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define Array
        values = [20, 10, 30]
        array_mobs = VGroup(*[

                Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1),
                Text(str(v), font_size=32)
            ) for v in values
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).center()

        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Define Gnome (Pointer)
        gnome = Triangle(color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2).rotate(PI)
        gnome.next_to(array_mobs[0], DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Step 2: Compare index 1 (10) and index 0 (20). Out of order!

Maintain a 'Current Min' label that updates whenever a smaller number is encountered, highlighting the new minimum in Blue and larger numbers in Grey during the comparison.

from manim import *

class FindMinValue(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Algorithm: Find Minimum Value", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Define Unsorted Array
        values = [35, 12, 56, 7, 24, 19]
        array_mobs = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                Square(side_length=0.9, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1),
                Text(str(v), font_size=28)
            ) for v in values
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).center()

        self.play(FadeIn(array_mobs))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Setup 'Current Min' Tracker
        min_val = values[0]
        # FIXED: Changed CYAN (undefined) to TEAL
        min_label_text = Text("Current Min: ", font_size=24, color=TEAL)
        min_val_mob = Text(str(min_val), font_size=32, color=TEAL)
        min_tracker_group = VGroup(min_label_text, min_val_mob).arrange(RIGHT).to_corner(UL, buff=1.0)

        self.play(Write(min_tracker_group))
        self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[0], color=TEAL))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 4. Search Loop
        pointer = Arrow(DOWN * 0.8, ORIGIN, color=TEAL).scale(0.7)
        pointer.next_to(array_mobs[0], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(pointer))

        for i in range(1, len(values)):
            # Move pointer
            self.play(pointer.animate.next_to(array_mobs[i], DOWN, buff=0.1), run_time=0.6)
            
            # Comparison highlight
            curr_val = values[i]
            self.play(Indicate(array_mobs[i][0], color=WHITE), run_time=0.4)

            if curr_val < min_val:
                # New Min Found!
                old_min_val = min_val
                max_val = curr_val # Logic remains same, but name is local
                min_val = curr_val
                new_min_mob = Text(str(min_val), font_size=32, color=BLUE).move_to(min_val_mob.get_center())
                
                self.play(
                    array_mobs[i][0].animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.4).set_color(BLUE),
                    Transform(min_val_mob, new_min_mob),
                    # Reset previous min box if it was colored
                    *[array_mobs[j][0].animate.set_fill(opacity=0.1).set_color(WHITE) 
                      for j in range(i) if values[j] == old_min_val]
                )
                self.play(Indicate(min_val_mob, scale_factor=1.3))
            else:
                # Not a new min
                self.play(array_mobs[i][0].animate.set_color(GREY_B), run_time=0.4)
                self.wait(0.2)
                self.play(array_mobs[i][0].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.2)

        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Final Result
        final_msg = Text(f"Minimum Value is {min_val}", font_size=32, color=BLUE).next_to(array_mobs, UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        self.play(Indicate(final_msg))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, array_mobs, min_tracker_group, pointer, final_msg)))

examples.instruction: Visualize the Constant Multiple Rule in calculus. Demonstrate that a constant coefficient 'c' can be pulled out of a derivative operator. Animate the expression d/dx [c * f(x)] transforming into c * d/dx [f(x)], using a distinct color for the constant to help the viewer track its movement.

from manim import *

class ConstantMultipleRule(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Calculus: Constant Multiple Rule", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Display the rule symbolically
        # FIXED: Removed tex_to_color_map to avoid collision with 'c' in '\frac'
        # We will color the parts manually by index for robustness.

        # Initial state: d/dx [c f(x)]
        # Indices: 0:\frac{d}{dx}, 1:[, 2:c, 3:f(x), 4:]
        initial = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", "[", "c", "f(x)", "]", font_size=60)
        initial[2].set_color(YELLOW) # color 'c'
        initial[3].set_color(GREEN)  # color 'f(x)'
        initial.move_to(ORIGIN)

        # Target state: c * d/dx [f(x)]
        # Indices: 0:c, 1:\frac{d}{dx}, 2:[, 3:f(x), 4:]
        target = MathTex("c", r"\frac{d}{dx}", "[", "f(x)", "]", font_size=60)
        target[0].set_color(YELLOW) # color 'c'
        target[3].set_color(GREEN)  # color 'f(x)'
        target.move_to(ORIGIN)

        # 3. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(initial))
        self.wait(1)

        # Highlight the constant 'c'
        self.play(Indicate(initial[2], color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Animate the constant 'pulling out' of the derivative
        # TransformMatchingTex will handle the movement of identical strings
        self.play(
            TransformMatchingTex(initial, target),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Show final rule form: c * f'(x)
        # Indices: 0:=, 1:c, 2:f'(x)
        final_form = MathTex("=", "c", "f'(x)", font_size=60)
        final_form[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        final_form[2].set_color(GREEN)
        final_form.next_to(target, RIGHT, buff=0.3)

        self.play(Write(final_form))
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(target, final_form), color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, target, final_form)))

examples.instruction: Visualize the concept of Text Outlining in Manim. Display the word 'OUTLINE' in a large, bold font. Animate the text starting with a solid fill and no border. Then, transform it to have a transparent fill and a thick, colorful stroke (outline). Finally, show both the fill and the stroke together to illustrate how they combine to create stylized typography.

from manim import *

class TextOutlineEffect(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Typography: Stroke and Outline", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Initial Solid Text
        # Bold font for better visibility of the outline later
        text = Text("OUTLINE", font_size=96, weight=BOLD, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Write(text))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Transition to Outline Only (No Fill)

        outline_only = text.copy()
        outline_only.set_fill(opacity=0)
        outline_only.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=4)

        subtitle1 = Text("Step 1: Stroke Only (No Fill)", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.2)

        self.play(
            Transform(text, outline_only),
            FadeIn(subtitle1, shift=UP),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Transition to Combined (Fill + Stroke)
        combined = outline_only.copy()
        combined.set_fill(BLUE_E, opacity=1.0)
        combined.set_stroke(WHITE, width=2)

        subtitle2 = Text("Step 2: Combined Fill and Stroke", font_size=24, color=WHITE).to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.2)

        self.play(
            Transform(text, combined),
            ReplacementTransform(subtitle1, subtitle2),
            run_time=2
        )

        # 5. Final highlight
        self.play(Indicate(text, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, text, subtitle2)))

examples.instruction: Visualize the relationship between Degrees and Radians in trigonometry. Animate an arc sweeping from 0 to 180 degrees. from manim import *
import numpy as np

class DegreeToRadian(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Degrees to Radians Equivalence", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Base Geometry
        center = ORIGIN + DOWN * 0.5
        base_line = Line(center, center + RIGHT * 3, color=WHITE)
        self.add(base_line)

        # 3. Animate Arc Sweeping to 180 degrees
        # We'll use a ValueTracker to coordinate the sweep and labels
        sweep_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=1.5,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=sweep_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES,
            arc_center=center,
            color=YELLOW
        ))
        
        moving_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            center, 
            center + rotate_vector(RIGHT * 3, sweep_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES),
            color=WHITE
        ))

        self.play(Create(arc), Create(moving_line))
        self.play(sweep_tracker.animate.set_value(180), run_time=2, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 4. Display 180 Degrees Label
        deg_label = MathTex("180^\\circ", font_size=48, color=YELLOW).next_to(arc, UP, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Write(deg_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Transform to Radians Label
        rad_label = MathTex("\\pi\\text{ radians}", font_size=48, color=GREEN).move_to(deg_label.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            Transform(deg_label, rad_label),
            arc.animate.set_color(GREEN),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 6. Show Equivalence Formula
        formula = MathTex("180^\\circ = \\pi\\text{ rad}", font_size=60, color=WHITE).to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.0)
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=YELLOW, buff=0.3)

        self.play(Create(box))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, base_line, arc, moving_line, deg_label, formula, box)))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class ReferenceAngleVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Trigonometry: Reference Angles", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Coordinate Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=8, y_length=6,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        ).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        self.play(Create(plane))

        # 3. Define the Terminal Side (150 degrees)
        angle_deg = 150
        angle_rad = angle_deg * DEGREES
        center = plane.coords_to_point(0, 0)
        terminal_side = Arrow(center, plane.coords_to_point(3 * np.cos(angle_rad), 3 * np.sin(angle_rad)), 
                              color=YELLOW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        terminal_label = Text("Terminal Side", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(terminal_side.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(terminal_side), Write(terminal_label))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 4. Show Standard Position Angle (150°)
        # Arc from 0 to 150
        main_arc = Arc(radius=1.0, start_angle=0, angle=angle_rad, arc_center=center, color=BLUE)
        # FIXED: Removed extra backslash in degree symbol
        main_label = MathTex("150^\\circ", font_size=36, color=BLUE).move_to(
            center + rotate_vector(RIGHT * 1.6, 75 * DEGREES)
        )

        self.play(Create(main_arc), Write(main_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Highlight Reference Angle (30°)
        # The reference angle is the acute angle to the x-axis
        # In QII, it is 180 - 150 = 30 degrees
        ref_arc = Arc(radius=1.0, start_angle=PI, angle=-30*DEGREES, arc_center=center, color=GREEN)
        # FIXED: Corrected TeX syntax for degree symbol in raw string
        ref_label = MathTex(r"\theta_{ref} = 30^\circ", font_size=32, color=GREEN).move_to(
            center + rotate_vector(LEFT * 2.2, -15 * DEGREES)
        )
        
        ref_desc = Text("Angle to the x-axis", font_size=24, color=GREEN).to_corner(DL, buff=1.0)

        self.play(Create(ref_arc), Write(ref_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(ref_desc, shift=UP))
        self.play(Indicate(ref_arc, color=GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, plane, terminal_side, terminal_label, main_arc, main_label, ref_arc, ref_label, ref_desc)))

examples.instruction: Visualize how a linear transformation matrix affects the standard basis vectors i-hat and j-hat. Display a coordinate plane with i-hat (1,0) in Red and j-hat (0,1) in Green. Animate them being transformed by a matrix that scales i-hat by 2 and j-hat by 1.5. Show the transformation matrix and the new positions of the basis vectors clearly.
examples.output:
from manim import *

class BasisVectorTransform(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = Text("Linear Transformation: Basis Vectors", font_size=36, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 2. Setup Coordinate Plane (without immediate shift)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-5, 5, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_numbers": True, "font_size": 20},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )

        # 3. Define standard basis vectors at ORIGIN
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color=RED)
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=RED).next_to(i_hat.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color=GREEN)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=GREEN).next_to(j_hat.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # 4. Define Transformed Vectors
        i_new = Vector([2, 0], color=RED)
        i_new_label = MathTex(r"M\hat{i}", color=RED).next_to(i_new.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        j_new = Vector([0, 1.5], color=GREEN)
        j_new_label = MathTex(r"M\hat{j}", color=GREEN).next_to(j_new.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # --- CRITICAL FIX: Group and shift everything together to keep alignment ---
        # We include plane and initial vectors/labels in the group to shift them down together
        system_group = VGroup(plane, i_hat, i_label, j_hat, j_label, i_new, i_new_label, j_new, j_new_label)
        system_group.shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Write(i_label))
        self.play(Create(j_hat), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Display Transformation Matrix
        matrix = Matrix([[2, 0], [0, 1.5]])
        matrix_label = MathTex("M = ", color=BLUE).next_to(matrix, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        matrix_group = VGroup(matrix_label, matrix).to_corner(UL, buff=0.6).scale(0.8)

        self.play(Write(matrix_group))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # 6. Animation: The Transformation
        self.play(
            Transform(i_hat, i_new),
            Transform(i_label, i_new_label),
            Transform(j_hat, j_new),
            Transform(j_label, j_new_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Highlight the columns of the matrix matching the results
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix.get_columns()[0], color=RED, buff=0.1)
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix.get_columns()[1], color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.play(Indicate(i_hat))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(col1_rect, col2_rect))
        self.play(Indicate(j_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        # Clear Scene
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, plane, i_hat, i_label, j_hat, j_label, matrix_group, col2_rect)))

examples.instruction: Visualize the concept of a tangent line to a circle. Draw a circle, a point on the circle, the radius to that point, and a tangent line perpendicular to the radius. Animate the point moving around the circle while the tangent line follows it.
examples.output:
from manim import *

class TangentLineVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        title = Text("Tangent Line to a Circle").to_edge(UP)
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color=BLUE)
        
        dot = Dot(circle.point_at_angle(0), color=RED)
        radius_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(ORIGIN, dot.get_center(), color=YELLOW))
        
        def get_tangent():
            angle = angle_of_vector(dot.get_center())
            p1 = dot.get_center() + rotate_vector(UP*1.5, angle)
            p2 = dot.get_center() + rotate_vector(DOWN*1.5, angle)
            return Line(p1, p2, color=RED)
            
        tangent_line = always_redraw(get_tangent)
        
        def get_right_angle():
            angle = angle_of_vector(dot.get_center())
            p0 = dot.get_center()
            dir_rad = rotate_vector(RIGHT, angle)
            dir_tan = rotate_vector(UP, angle)
            p1 = p0 - dir_rad * 0.3
            p2 = p1 + dir_tan * 0.3
            p3 = p0 + dir_tan * 0.3
            return VGroup(Line(p1, p2, color=WHITE), Line(p2, p3, color=WHITE))
            
        right_angle = always_redraw(get_right_angle)

        self.play(Write(title), Create(circle))
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(radius_line), Create(tangent_line))
        self.play(Create(right_angle))
        
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, circle), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class SineAndCosecant(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        title = Text("Trigonometry: Sine and Cosecant", font_size=40).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(title))
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2], y_range=[-3, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        sin_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=BLUE)
        sin_label = MathTex(r"y = \sin(x)", color=BLUE).next_to(axes, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(sin_graph), Write(sin_label))
        
        x_min = float(np.arcsin(1/3))
        csc_graph_pos = axes.plot(lambda x: 1/np.sin(x), x_range=[x_min, PI-x_min], color=YELLOW)
        csc_graph_neg = axes.plot(lambda x: 1/np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI+x_min, -x_min], color=YELLOW)
        
        csc_label = MathTex(r"y = \csc(x)", color=YELLOW).next_to(sin_label, RIGHT, buff=1)
        
        asymp1 = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, -3), axes.c2p(0, 3), color=GRAY)
        asymp2 = DashedLine(axes.c2p(PI, -3), axes.c2p(PI, 3), color=GRAY)
        asymp3 = DashedLine(axes.c2p(-PI, -3), axes.c2p(-PI, 3), color=GRAY)
        
        self.play(Create(asymp1), Create(asymp2), Create(asymp3))
        self.play(Create(csc_graph_pos), Create(csc_graph_neg), Write(csc_label))
        self.wait(2)
